correctness.rationale: All assumptions are explicit: n≥1, nontrivial finite C with d(C)≤n inside an existentially closed exponent-three group; class at most three and finite local freeness. The first defect rank r₂=dim((C∩γ₂(G))/γ₂(C))≤dim gr₁(C)≤n, so q₂(n) fresh rank supplies r₂ independent degree-two wedges. In the PRIMARY source Lemma 4.7 proof, Claim B uses only independence to force all degree-two relation coefficients to zero, and Claim C uses the direct-sum V_G⊗Λ²V_F component and independence to force all old-side commutator coefficients to zero; overlap of pairs within the fresh basis does not affect either argument. Lemma 4.8 then obtains degree-two strictness. With N=n+q₂(n), the second defect r₃≤dim gr₂(D₁)≤binom(N,2). Independent triple-wedge basis classes in F_{q₃(N)} ensure central relations give G∩L=1 by the exact argument of primary Lemma 4.9. The intersection computations in Lemma 4.10 need only that each central defect is represented by a degree-three generator; a shared fresh factor suffices. Primary Lemma 4.6 adds exactly two generators, and finite exponent-three groups are locally finite, allowing e.c. transfer into M. Theorems 3.3 and Proposition 4.13 then give B(s(m)). Independent reimplementation computed q₂,q₃,B for n=1,2,3,4,5,10,100,1000,10000,100000 and s(m),B(s(m)) for m=1,2,3,5,10,20,40,100; no numerical contradiction. The universal bound rests on the symbolic proof, not a finite sample.

value.rationale: The object is the natural strict finite envelope of a finite subgroup of an existentially closed exponent-three group, a central quantitative input in the primary model-companion proof. Existing constructions use distinct commutator blocks and a quadratic generator bound; the independently motivated invariant is the number of new generators required to cure first- and second-layer defects. Packing through Λ² and Λ³ systematically improves the asymptotic generator bound from 15n² to n+O(n^(2/3)), and the concrete downstream finite-amalgamation obstruction witness from O(m⁸) to O(m⁴). The improvement is structural and asymptotic, not a renaming or tiny-table computation. The source itself explicitly highlights nonoptimality, but does not present this uniform propagation. No optimality or complexity lower bound is claimed.
